scope: Three current design/code contradictions and faithful early v1 IT port timing. No story/AC edits, PO/QA approval or runtime PASS.

decisions.actualSeam: GuidedRuntime callback is closed code-only BridgeOutcome; GuidedJournal consumes SHA256 metadata lines only. These are strong no-value controls but do not provide the named free-text journal/callback sinks for the required dynamic redactor oracle.
decisions.decision: Add optional top-level errorMessage:string to existing BridgeOutcome, already redacted and bounded1..2048 characters; worker additionally caps final UTF-8 diagnostic bytes at2048. Admit it only for an actual failed/uncertain consumed action, never SUCCEEDED/OK, and never change outcome/state. Leave ledger/action/admission digest and publication authority unchanged. This exact callback.errorMessage spelling matches AC10.
decisions.pipeline: Capture actual runtime/native failure before redaction in a test-only in-memory observation seam; run the redactor built from actual resolved secretValues and known values before any truncation, interpolation, serialization, diagnostic file write, stderr or callback. Then bound bytes and create the closed diagnostic. Never stringify the secret-bearing dispatch frame or raw exception wholesale. No new secret-bearing channel is added: only already-redacted text goes on the existing outcome channel.
decisions.journal: Keep GuidedJournal and its owner/consumption hashes untouched. Add a distinct per-session diagnostic JSONL file with closed safe identity+already-redacted errorMessage records, restrictive file permissions and finite session record/byte budgets. This file is not read by consume/recovery, cannot restore/retry a context, cannot affect admission, and cannot retroactively change a completed success. Diagnostic write failure must not alter an already determined action verdict.
decisions.oracleRequirements: Injected hook must contain the actual released canary and produce REDACTED in every implemented free-text sink. C-6 separately captures actual native Playwright error bytes before redaction; native capture and injected-hook evidence must be labelled separately. Scan stdout/stderr/relay/failure/manifest/callbacks/diagnostic journal/parent log with real runtime effects. No absent sink or unit redactor alone earns a joined oracle PASS. Native C6 raw-error evidence must satisfy its actual canary-containing native-error assertion; an injected error hook cannot be relabelled as Playwright raw bytes. If a native message lacks the canary, record that result honestly and obtain independent acceptance disposition rather than inventing it.

decisions.poAmendment: Clarify AC10/C6 sink names and authority separation. Preserve actual canary/raw-error/redactor requirements; adding the bounded optional diagnostic supplies the requested sink rather than weakening proof.

decisions.actualSeam: GuidedSessionService.consume commits DISPATCHING/dispatchCount1 before resolving. AlreadyConsumed is returned for duplicate/consumed admissions. GuidedDispatchService returns that ledger before resolve or send; WonConsumption is never cached. Runner consumption and permanent owner journal likewise prevent reconstitution/resend.
decisions.decision: Split legitimate pre-consume recovery from post-consume uncertainty. A controller crash after prepare/admit but before consume leaves ADMITTED/count0: if the same worker/context/proof remains live and fresh, recovery may re-enter consume, resolve once and send once. A crash after committed consume never resolves or sends again; bounded recovery records uncertainty using the existing ledger/reaper, not replay.

executedOraclePlan.case: Crash after ADMITTED commit, before consume
executedOraclePlan.after: One winning consume, one actual Vault read, one dispatch at most; current mayUse/origin/evidence rechecks remain required.

executedOraclePlan.case: Crash after consumed commit, before resolve
executedOraclePlan.after: AlreadyConsumed; no read, no send; no fabricated release row. Outcome remains uncertain until bounded reconciliation.

executedOraclePlan.case: Crash after resolve, before/after ambiguous send
executedOraclePlan.before: One actual resolution; send count reflects the actual fault location, never guessed
executedOraclePlan.after: No new read/send. Resolved scope erased; safe decision metadata only; known failure/success preserved and unobserved effects remain uncertain.

decisions.forbidden: Never perform read-and-discard to manufacture the old counter assertion. Never retain WonConsumption or a value-bearing frame in an outbox/retry store. Never create a new worker/browser replay after context loss to satisfy pre-consume recovery.
decisions.contractRows: No new wire shape required; core at-most-once/closed ledger contracts remain unchanged.
decisions.poAmendment: Replace the contradictory C4 post-consume re-resolution sentence with the three falsifiable fault positions. Keep ordinary observed replay definite-refusal/outage fresh-attempt re-resolution tests and C5 TRACE capture over those sub-runs; do not weaken any security invariant.

decisions.actualSeam: Current runner uses one cancellation path for cancellation/revocation/fail-closed control loss. Backend currently accepts ERROR/CANCELLED only against cancel_requested_at; a runtime merely naming an API code cannot assign it.
decisions.decision: Keep AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED an API-assigned cause. Before any send, the dispatcher records its own denied-authority terminal ERROR/AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED. For a running execution, map only a terminal runner ERROR/CANCELLED with independently stored revoked_at to API ERROR/AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED; never map a runner-supplied AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED string directly. A recorded user cancel retains ERROR/CANCELLED precedence when both facts exist; revocation audit remains recorded independently. Control/network denial without either trusted fact remains an unmapped cancellation diagnostic.
decisions.preservation: PASSED or FAILED reports/previous terminal outcomes are not rewritten because a later revocation/cancel flag exists. A fill already in flight retains the stated one-poll-plus-one-step residual. Guided explicit authorization denial continues stop{REVOKED}/SECRET_USE_REVOKED; ledger/API/audit causes are distinguished.
decisions.oracleRequirements: Compare pre-send denial, live recorded revocation, user cancellation, both flags, missing flags, spoofed API code, completed PASS, completed FAILED/LOGIN_REQUIRED and late control arrival. Retain result/evidence independence, write-once revoked_at and unique REVOKED_MID_RUN audit.
decisions.poAmendment: Clarify AC13 cause timing and preservation/precedence; add no runner API-code privilege and weaken no stop bound.
decisions.laneBConfirmation: B confirmed user-cancel priority when both timestamps exist, only revoked_at maps AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED, missing trusted facts unmapped, and PASSED/FAILED unchanged. Synchronous recheck skips already terminal owners without fresh mayUse/audit.
